page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, no margin notes. Running head at top right, chapter number at top left. Catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: vel ἐπιτρόπῳ[?] in docendo nominari & usurpari seuerisimè vetuerit. Theodoret.libr.2. Hist.cap. 27. Unde longius progredi prohibita, & ipso Aetianorum nomine damnata, nouis tamen & interpolatis Eunomaniorum, & Eudoxianorū appellationibus retenta, & velut crambe recocta reposita est, tam est in se simulando Satan astutus artifex. Asia igitur quæ minor est, imprimis item à Tauro monte ad Hellespontum, Cappadocia, Paphlagonia, & Cilicia, unà cum Constantinopolitano tractu hac peste grauissimè laborauit, Sozomen.lib.6.cap.27. quæ Basilij Magni, & Gregorij Nazianzeni eruditissimis disputationibus, tanquam salubribus medicamentis, non tam sanata prorsus est, quàm ad tempus repressa. Hic autem Aetius tanti mali seminator patre Georgio milite natus est Antiochiæ, unde Syrus dictus non Cilix, vt Epiphanius tamen putat, sed eum refutat Sozom. lib.6. cap.26. alius ab Alexandrino & Ægyptio, quem refert Suidas etiam Arianam hærefin amplexum esse. Propter summam autem paupertatem hic noster primum χρυσοχοΐαν[?], vt omnes tradunt, exercuit, deinde Paulino Antiocheno Episcopo defuncto, spem adipiscendi aliquando Episcopatus magna animi ambitione & ingenij confidentia concipiens se Leontio Paulini successori adiunxit, à quo Diaconus Ecclesiæ factus, non autem à Georgio Alexandrino Episcopo (in quo hallucinatur Epiphanius, vt ex Suida facile intelligi potest. Nam duos Aetios confundit Epiphanius) inepta quædam & blasphema contra Christum Dei filium euomere[?]

page.notes: Greek word after "vel" and "primum" is partly doubtful (ἐπιτρόπῳ, χρυσοχοΐαν). "euomere" is read from a slightly blurred line. Catchword "cœpit" is set at lower right. Chapter number "Cap.54." is taken as the printed head number on the left. Unclear Greek accents are not certain.
